ideas.risks: The proof may fail because the update scheme enforces a strong stability notion on all rounds; adaptive adversaries may still violate it on hard distributions. Tracking γ_t under finite-sample estimation noise is delicate.
ideas.summary: Investigate a concrete residual-filter family where each round forms\n\(D_{t+1}(x) \propto D_t(x)\,\phi_t(|h_t(x)-y|)\) with clipping + renormalization, and prove explicit invariants: (i) \(\Pr_{D_t}[\phi_t\neq 0]\ge 1/\mathrm{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon)\), (ii) \(\mathrm{OPT}_C(D_t)\le 1/2-\gamma_t\) where \(\gamma_t\) is a computable lower bound from observable quantities. Then instantiate an (α,γ)-boosting theorem in the fixed-slack oracle regime.
ideas.title: Conditional positive route via clipping-stable residual filters
ideas.why_promising: If the invariants hold, the open blocker is removed directly and the existing strong candidate template becomes runnable.

ideas.risks: Constructing a quantified counterexample is hard; may require tailoring both class and distributions to an adaptive filter that is natural rather than pathological. Could collapse into trivialities if filter is disallowed by implementation constraints.
ideas.summary: Build a formal \((C,D,F)\) witness with small \(\mathrm{OPT}_C(D)\) but where adaptive reweighting used by plausible wrappers drives \(\mathrm{OPT}_C(D_t)\to 1/2\) in finite rounds or causes exponential support collapse. Candidate class could be a planted-bi-structure where labels are unambiguous on rare regions and ambiguous on high-residual regions; then filtering on residual amplifies ambiguity.
ideas.title: Explicit adaptive filter obstruction for weak-to-strong conversion
ideas.why_promising: A quantified obstruction would immediately explain why any generic wrapper is impossible without extra assumptions and set a sharp boundary for conditional positive theorems.

ideas.risks: Theorems in the literature may use different normalization (correlation vs excess risk) and strong assumptions (realizability, margin, noise conditions) that are easy to miss. Hidden constants can invalidate claimed polynomial dependence on \(1/\epsilon\).
ideas.summary: Create a theorem-by-theorem translation table for KMV08, Feldman, and potential-based agnostic boosting into the atlas oracle form (binary 0/1 output, guarantee \(\mathrm{err}\le\mathrm{OPT}+\beta\), distribution-free). Record exact dependence on \(\beta,\gamma,\delta,1/\epsilon,1/\mu_t\).
ideas.title: Oracle-semantics and parameter translation audit for existing boosters
ideas.why_promising: A precise compatibility table will convert current ambiguity into either a valid theorem, or a principled lower bound on what the fixed-slack wrapper can and cannot achieve.

ideas.risks: SQ lower bounds often depend on response precision and tolerances; mapping the fixed-slack learner exactly to query accuracy may overconstrain and become vacuous. Could be conditional on cryptographic/randomness assumptions.
ideas.summary: Formalize fixed-slack weak oracle as an SQ oracle with precision \(\tau\approx 1/2-\beta\), then prove that this precision is insufficient to simulate arbitrary-\(\epsilon\) agnostic weak-boosting in polynomial time for certain classes under known hard-to-amplify SQ families. Identify whether this yields a true separation under average-case or planted-noise assumptions.
ideas.title: SQ-precision barrier to arbitrary-ε amplification
ideas.why_promising: Could produce a principled conditional negative route (hardness) that is independent of specific reduction artifacts and clarifies whether the blocker is information-theoretic/communication-like rather than algorithmic.

ideas.risks: May require additional structure that is too strong for target class and makes results less impactful. Could revert to proper learning or assume access to confidence scores not present in the oracle.
ideas.summary: Pursue a conditional theorem under explicit stability/margin conditions (e.g., Tsybakov noise + bounded label-noise under residual filters, or exp-concave losses induced by residuals) and prove fixed-slack closure to \(\epsilon\)-agnostic under these assumptions. Make assumptions minimal and check compatibility with known classes.
ideas.title: Conditional positive theorem under stability/noise regularity
ideas.why_promising: May deliver the strongest next publishable theorem: a true implication with realistic assumptions and quantified bounds, which can later delimit maximal generality.

ideas.risks: Could become algorithmically heavy and difficult to prove efficient in the general model; complexity may hide by-large constants in entropy- or dimension-dependent terms.
ideas.summary: Recast wrappers as minimax game between learner and filter and derive a mirror-descent or multiplicative-weights interpretation. Try to show either (a) guaranteed decrease in a convex potential that enforces the two invariants, or (b) derive impossibility when the potential cannot be bounded due to adversarial residual geometry.
ideas.title: Game-theoretic potential for residual-forcing wrapper
ideas.why_promising: Potential-based proofs often convert ad hoc adaptive filtering into clean invariants; if successful, gives both existence and explicit γ_t/mass recurrences.
